name: The First Sliver

abilities.text: Sliver spells you cast have cascade.

notes: The printed Cascade line is the `cascade` declaration (covers). The grant to Sliver spells is written as the cast trigger the granted ability IS (CR 702.85a), filtered on the Sliver subtype — a Sliver spell is any spell with the Sliver subtype, creature or Kindred. The script format cannot attach an ability to a spell on the stack (`grant-ability` scope is battlefield permanents). Known engine shortfall: the core `cascade` op reads the mana value of the ability's SOURCE (The First Sliver, MV 7) rather than of the Sliver spell just cast.

issues: Sliver spells you cast have cascade. — expected Each Sliver spell you cast cascades off ITS OWN mana value — cast Metallic Sliver (MV 1) and you exile until a nonland card of MV 0. — scripted {op:'cascade'} on a trigger sourced by The First Sliver (MV 7); src/engine/game.ts:1241 uses src.def.manaValue, so every granted cascade exiles until a nonland card of MV <= 6 no matter how cheap the Sliver was. Massively too generous, and wrong in the opposite direction from Imoti. — CR 702.85a

Sliver spells you cast have cascade. — expected A discriminating test would cast a cheap Sliver over a library whose top nonland card has MV between the Sliver's MV and 7. — scripted Blind scenario 2 casts Metallic Sliver (MV 1) over Ornithopter (MV 0). MV 0 < 1 and MV 0 < 7, so it passes identically under correct and buggy semantics — the 3/3 pass does not clear this line. Scenario 1 tests only the printed cascade:true; scenario 3 tests only the negative subtype filter. — CR 702.85a

Sliver spells you cast have cascade. — expected "Sliver spells" = any spell with the Sliver subtype (creature or Kindred/Tribal). — scripted filter.subtypes=['Sliver'] — this part is correct, and the negative case is covered by scenario 3. — CR 702.85a

Cascade (… You may cast it without paying its mana cost …) — expected Casting the exiled card is optional. — scripted The cascade op casts unconditionally with no ask; the scenario's {answer:true} step is not consumed by cascade. Engine-wide shortfall affecting both the printed and granted cascade. — CR 702.85a
